result.title: Target-Free Autocalibration of Stereo PIV Camera Systems via Persistent-State Motion Representations
result.summary: Stereo Particle Image Velocimetry (PIV) recovers three-component velocity fields by triangulating tracer particles observed by synchronized cameras. It requires an accurate extrinsic calibration, which is still obtained by inserting a physical target into the flow and must be repeated whenever the rig is moved. We present a target-free method that calibrates a stereo PIV rig directly from particle image sequences. Because tracer particles are visually indistinguishable, we match motion rather than appearance: building on CUT3R, each camera stream is processed by a recurrent transformer whose persistent state accumulates particle motion over time. The state is decoded into per-camera optical flow and queried by a cross-view decoder that regresses bidirectional point correspondences, from which the relative pose is recovered with a five-point RANSAC solver. We train on a new synthetic stereo PIV dataset with ground-truth poses and evaluate on standard PIV optical flow benchmarks and on 200 real rig placements. Our model achieves lower flow error than existing PIV networks, more accurate cross-view correspondences than COTR, and higher pose accuracy than the strongest detector-matcher pipelines on both synthetic and real data, without any calibration target.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出一种无需标定靶的立体 PIV 相机自标定方法：用循环 transformer 逐路累积粒子运动形成持久状态，解码为光流并由跨视角解码器回归双向点对应，再用五点 RANSAC 恢复相对位姿。
AI.relevance_reason: 以「匹配运动而非外观」的持久状态累积与跨视角查询解码，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据如何在内部状态中长期保留并被下游读出的问题提供可供核查的架构线索；但领域相距较远，可迁移性需阅读原文判断。
